Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it down into smaller, simpler versions of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a base case—a condition that stops the recursion and prevents infinite loops. When the base case isn't met, the function makes a recursive call with modified input, moving closer to that stopping point. The results from each recursive call then bubble back up and combine to produce the final answer.
